import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker
import io

# Load the dataset from the string
csv_data = """survived,pclass,sex,age,sibsp,parch,fare,embarked,class,who,adult_male,deck,embark_town,alive,alone
0,3,male,22.0,1,0,7.25,S,Third,man,True,,Southampton,no,False
1,1,female,38.0,1,0,71.2833,C,First,woman,False,C,Cherbourg,yes,False
1,3,female,26.0,0,0,7.925,S,Third,woman,False,,Southampton,yes,True
1,1,female,35.0,1,0,53.1,S,First,woman,False,C,Southampton,yes,False
0,3,male,35.0,0,0,8.05,S,Third,man,True,,Southampton,no,True
"""

df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(csv_data))

# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create a figure and axes for the plot
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 7))
ax = plt.gca()

# Create the bar plot
# We visualize the survival rate (mean of 'survived' column) broken down by passenger class and sex.
# The 'order' parameter ensures the x-axis is correctly sorted.
# The 'palette' provides a color-blind friendly color scheme.
plot = sns.barplot(
    data=df,
    x='class',
    y='survived',
    hue='sex',
    order=['First', 'Second', 'Third'],
    palette='viridis',
    ax=ax
)

# --- Customize the plot for clarity and impact ---

# Set a clear and descriptive title
ax.set_title(
    'Titanic Survival Rate by Passenger Class and Sex',
    fontsize=18,
    fontweight='bold',
    pad=20
)

# Set informative labels for the axes
ax.set_xlabel('Passenger Class', fontsize=14, labelpad=15)
ax.set_ylabel('Survival Rate', fontsize=14, labelpad=15)

# Format the y-axis to show percentages
ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(mticker.PercentFormatter(xmax=1.0))
ax.set_ylim(0, 1.1) # Set y-limit to 110% to give space for annotations

# Add annotations (percentage labels) on top of each bar
for p in ax.patches:
    height = p.get_height()
    if pd.notna(height) and height > 0:
        ax.annotate(
            f'{height:.0%}',
            (p.get_x() + p.get_width() / 2., height),
            ha='center',
            va='center',
            xytext=(0, 9),
            textcoords='offset points',
            fontsize=12,
            fontweight='semibold'
        )

# Customize the legend
ax.legend(title='Sex', title_fontsize='13', fontsize='12', frameon=True, shadow=True)

# Improve layout and remove unnecessary spines
sns.despine(left=True)
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the resulting plot to a file
plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')

# Close the plot to free up memory
plt.close()
